verses.ar: اَلذُّبَابُ ٱلْمَيِّتُ يُنَتِّنُ وَيُخَمِّرُ طِيبَ ٱلْعَطَّارِ. جَهَالَةٌ قَلِيلَةٌ أَثْقَلُ مِنَ ٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَمِنَ ٱلْكَرَامَةِ.
verses.kjv: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: [so doth] a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom [and] honour.
verses.web: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

verses.ar: قَلْبُ ٱلْحَكِيمِ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ، وَقَلْبُ ٱلْجَاهِلِ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ.
verses.kjv: A wise man’s heart [is] at his right hand; but a fool’s heart at his left.
verses.web: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.

verses.ar: أَيْضًا إِذَا مَشَى ٱلْجَاهِلُ فِي ٱلطَّرِيقِ يَنْقُصُ فَهْمُهُ، وَيَقُولُ لِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ: إِنَّهُ جَاهِلٌ.
verses.kjv: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth [him], and he saith to every one [that] he [is] a fool.
verses.web: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.

verses.ar: إِنْ صَعِدَتْ عَلَيْكَ رُوحُ ٱلْمُتَسَلِّطِ، فَلَا تَتْرُكْ مَكَانَكَ، لِأَنَّ ٱلْهُدُوءَ يُسَكِّنُ خَطَايَا عَظِيمَةً.
verses.kjv: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
verses.web: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

verses.ar: يُوجَدُ شَرٌّ رَأَيْتُهُ تَحْتَ ٱلشَّمْسِ، كَسَهْوٍ صَادِرٍ مِنْ قِبَلِ ٱلْمُتَسَلِّطِ:
verses.kjv: There is an evil [which] I have seen under the sun, as an error [which] proceedeth from the ruler:
verses.web: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.

verses.ar: ٱلْجَهَالَةُ جُعِلَتْ فِي مَعَالِيَ كَثِيرَةٍ، وَٱلْأَغْنِيَاءُ يَجْلِسُونَ فِي ٱلسَّافِلِ.
verses.kjv: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.web: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

verses.ar: قَدْ رَأَيْتُ عَبِيدًا عَلَى ٱلْخَيْلِ، وَرُؤَسَاءَ مَاشِينَ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ كَٱلْعَبِيدِ.
verses.kjv: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.web: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

verses.ar: مَنْ يَحْفُرْ هُوَّةً يَقَعْ فِيهَا، وَمَنْ يَنْقُضْ جِدَارًا تَلْدَغْهُ حَيَّةٌ.
verses.kjv: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.web: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

verses.ar: مَنْ يَقْلَعْ حِجَارَةً يُوجَعْ بِهَا. مَنْ يُشَقِّقُ حَطَبًا يَكُونُ فِي خَطَرٍ مِنْهُ.
verses.kjv: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; [and] he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
verses.web: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.

verses.ar: إِنْ كَلَّ ٱلْحَدِيدُ وَلَمْ يُسَنِّنْ هُوَ حَدَّهُ، فَلْيَزِدِ ٱلْقُوَّةَ. أَمَّا ٱلْحِكْمَةُ فَنَافِعَةٌ لِلْإِنْجَاحِ.
verses.kjv: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom [is] profitable to direct.
verses.web: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

verses.ar: إِنْ لَدَغَتِ ٱلْحَيَّةُ بِلَا رُقْيَةٍ، فَلَا مَنْفَعَةَ لِلرَّاقِي.
verses.kjv: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
verses.web: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.

verses.ar: كَلِمَاتُ فَمِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ نِعْمَةٌ، وَشَفَتَا ٱلْجَاهِلِ تَبْتَلِعَانِهِ.
verses.kjv: The words of a wise man’s mouth [are] gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
verses.web: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.

verses.ar: اِبْتِدَاءُ كَلَامِ فَمِهِ جَهَالَةٌ، وَآخِرُ فَمِهِ جُنُونٌ رَدِيءٌ.
verses.kjv: The beginning of the words of his mouth [is] foolishness: and the end of his talk [is] mischievous madness.
verses.web: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

verses.ar: وَٱلْجَاهِلُ يُكَثِّرُ ٱلْكَلَامَ. لَا يَعْلَمُ إِنْسَانٌ مَا يَكُونُ. وَمَاذَا يَصِيرُ بَعْدَهُ مَنْ يُخْبِرُهُ؟
verses.kjv: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
verses.web: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?

verses.ar: تَعَبُ ٱلْجُهَلَاءِ يُعْيِيهِمْ، لِأَنَّهُ لَا يَعْلَمُ كَيْفَ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ
verses.kjv: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
verses.web: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.

verses.ar: وَيْلٌ لَكِ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْأَرْضُ إِذَا كَانَ مَلِكُكِ وَلَدًا، وَرُؤَسَاؤُكِ يَأْكُلُونَ فِي ٱلصَّبَاحِ.
verses.kjv: ¶ Woe to thee, O land, when thy king [is] a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
verses.web: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!

verses.ar: طُوبَى لَكِ أَيَّتُهَا ٱلْأَرْضُ إِذَا كَانَ مَلِكُكِ ٱبْنَ شُرَفَاءَ، وَرُؤَسَاؤُكِ يَأْكُلُونَ فِي ٱلْوَقْتِ لِلْقُوَّةِ لَا لِلسُّكْرِ.
verses.kjv: Blessed [art] thou, O land, when thy king [is] the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.web: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

verses.ar: بِٱلْكَسَلِ ٱلْكَثِيرِ يَهْبِطُ ٱلسَّقْفُ، وَبِتَدَلِّي ٱلْيَدَيْنِ يَكِفُ ٱلْبَيْتُ.
verses.kjv: ¶ By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
verses.web: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

verses.ar: لِلْضَّحِكِ يَعْمَلُونَ وَلِيمَةً، وَٱلْخَمْرُ تُفَرِّحُ ٱلْعَيْشَ. أَمَّا ٱلْفِضَّةُ فَتُحَصِّلُ ٱلْكُلَّ.
verses.kjv: ¶ A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all [things].
verses.web: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.

verses.ar: لَا تَسُبَّ ٱلْمَلِكَ وَلَا فِي فِكْرِكَ، وَلَا تَسُبَّ ٱلْغَنِيَّ فِي مَضْجَعِكَ، لِأَنَّ طَيْرَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ يَنْقُلُ ٱلصَّوْتَ، وَذُو ٱلْجَنَاحِ يُخْبِرُ بِٱلْأَمْرِ.
verses.kjv: ¶ Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
verses.web: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
